pointers.sentence: Some of the test command's options are not its own: the runner's class adds them, and the class may be named on the same command line (`django/core/management/commands/test.py:Command`).

`BaseCommand.run_from_argv` builds the parser before it parses ([Running a command: `BaseCommand`](../commands/running.md)), so `Command.run_from_argv` first reads `--testrunner` alone, with `get_command_line_option`; its docstring gives the reason, that this lets a runner define further options (`django/core/management/commands/test.py:Command.run_from_argv`).

`Command.add_arguments` adds the labels, `--noinput` and `--testrunner`, and takes the class with `get_runner`, which imports the module of the dotted path read, or of `TEST_RUNNER`, and returns the attribute the last part names (`django/test/utils.py:get_runner`); if the class has an `add_arguments`, it adds its options.

`Command.handle` takes the class again, from the parsed option or the setting; replaces a `--parallel` of `"auto"` by what `get_max_test_processes` returns ([Running in parallel: `ParallelTestSuite`](parallel.md)); makes the runner with every option as a keyword argument, those every command shares included; calls `run_tests` with the labels, timed as `"Total run"`; and calls `sys.exit` with 1 if it returned a true value, such as a count above zero (`django/core/management/commands/test.py:Command.handle`).
`DiscoverRunner.add_arguments`, a class method, runs before any runner exists; `DiscoverRunner.__init__` keeps most options under their destinations (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.__init__`).
`--pdb` with a `parallel` above 1 is refused with `ValueError`; Django's documentation says a debugger there ends in `bdb.BdbQuit` (`docs/ref/django-admin.txt`).
`DiscoverRunner.run_tests` calls the runner's own methods in a fixed order (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.run_tests`):
Django's documentation lets a project's runner subclass `DiscoverRunner` or stand alone, and asks it to accept `**kwargs`, so that Django can add options (`docs/topics/testing/advanced.txt`).

`DiscoverRunner.run_checks` calls the check command with the runner's verbosity and the aliases the tests use, after the databases since, its comment says, some checks need them (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.run_checks`).

The checks tagged for databases run on those aliases; with none, as when no test names a database, they are left out (`django/core/checks/registry.py:CheckRegistry.run_checks`; [The system checks](../commands/checks.md)).
It runs the suite and, in a `finally`, logs the shuffle seed that `DiscoverRunner.setup_shuffler` logged before (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.run_suite`).

The runner's own lines go through `DiscoverRunner.log`: to a logger the runner was given, or else printed to standard output, INFO and above at verbosity 1, everything at 2 (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.log`).

`get_resultclass` returns `DebugSQLTextTestResult` with `--debug-sql`, else `PDBDebugResult` with `--pdb`, else `None`, which leaves `unittest.TextTestResult`; given both options, no debugger opens (`django/test/runner.py:DiscoverRunner.get_resultclass`).
`PDBDebugResult` opens a post-mortem debugger at each error, failure and failing subtest: ipdb where it can be imported, pdb otherwise (`django/test/runner.py:PDBDebugResult`).

`DebugSQLTextTestResult` sets the logger `"django.db.backends"` to DEBUG and, from `DebugSQLTextTestResult.startTest` to `DebugSQLTextTestResult.stopTest`, gives it a handler that writes into a string through `QueryFormatter` (`django/test/runner.py:DebugSQLTextTestResult`).
`QueryFormatter` passes each statement through its alias's `BaseDatabaseOperations.format_debug_sql`, which reindents it with sqlparse (`django/test/runner.py:QueryFormatter`).

`TimeKeeper.timed` records its block's time under a name entered as the block begins, so a block is printed before those inside it, such as each creation `setup_databases` times (`django/test/utils.py:TimeKeeper`).
